sources_read: .qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r6/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks row 44; Internal Quality Checks row 44 with Mukesh annotation; rows 41-43 for context; Deterministic Checks check-scoring-policy/check-rubric-schema)
evidence:
Static weight audit of frozen task (.qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r6/task). Dimension weights: tests/scoring.toml [weights] functional=0.6, polish=0.2, visual=0.2, gates render/constraints=0.0, floor functional=0.05 (sha256 95f70d6e...bbba); byte-identical to the frozen template rules/projects/webdev-task-template/tests/scoring.toml (diff empty) and to the SKILL delivery profile ('functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2') and the Internal Quality Checks row 44 annotation ('Functionality has 60 pecent, and itself in functionality we define own verifer weightage'). No weight key in any [judge] block (parsed all five judge.toml with tomllib). score.py computes sum(w*score)/sum(w) over [weights] only, so judge.toml criterion weights act only within a dimension (weighted_mean).
Per-criterion weights (parsed): functional 43 binary criteria, total 58.5 (sha cfb70942...2b26). Highest 2.5: hro_stale_refused (refusal naming who changed the card - brief para 2 'tell me who'), hro_live_board (15-second live board, brief para 3), hro_candidate_private (no notes/reasons/others leak, brief para 5 'must never see'). 2.0: refused_put_back, bulk_all_or_none, undo_restores, undo_conflict, thread_earlier, unread_counts, unread_scrolled_up, drafts - all the brief's explicitly 'hard part' concurrency/conversation promises. Lowest 0.5: hro_job_open, hro_add_candidate, hro_reject_hired, hro_undo_full, hro_activity_refusals, hro_candidate_linked. The two basic CRUD rows are low because opening a job and adding a candidate with independent-context readback are already required by the constraints gate (tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:23) and the functional global browser gate (tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:11), and are prerequisites of many weighted rows; the others are narrow edge refusals or a single link. So within functional, weight tracks headline brief promises over setup/edge cases - honest.
Polish: 5 binary criteria, total 12 (live_board preservation 3, live_thread 3, session_resume 2.5, earlier_place 2, failed_send 1.5). All are browser-observed behaviours (draft/focus/scroll preservation, failed send, signed-out draft privacy) from brief paras 3-4, not style; the template's polish slot (responsive/a11y/feedback) is replaced by behavioural robustness, so the polish 0.2 is not style mass. Visual: 5 likert(points=5) criteria at equal weight 1.2 (total 6) - pure style, capped at 0.2 of reward.
Max non-functional contribution sanity check: style-only (visual) can contribute at most 0.2; polish (behavioural) 0.2; functional 0.6. Weak-app attempt: a beautiful app that passes both gates (real job+candidate persistence) and barely clears the 0.05 floor (~3 weight units, e.g. two trivial rows) scores at most 0.6*0.051+0.2*polish+0.2 - with dead live updates polish rows are 0 (each requires an update to arrive within 15 s), so ~0.23, below any app that implements the concurrency core (functional >=0.5 gives >=0.3 before visual). No inversion found where style outweighs functionality at dimension level. Conforming-alternative attempt: weights do not alter pass/fail of a conforming app, so no unfair loss from weighting.
Note (not a defect, template-controlled): because functional is split across 43 criteria, a single visual likert criterion (0.2*1.2/6=0.04 of reward) and the top polish rows (0.05) are each worth more than the highest functional criterion (0.6*2.5/58.5=0.0256); aggregate functionality still dominates 0.6 vs 0.2 style, and dimension weights are frozen by template/delivery profile, so this is recorded only. No runtime ranking/discrimination evidence exists (raw-evidence-index.json scope: 'reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'); this row's honesty judgement is static and does not depend on it, but measured monotonicity belongs to row 42 and remains unmeasured. No Oracle, model or portal score is claimed.
